October 1, 2026 / 12:12 PM EDT / CBS News Lisdoonvarna, Ireland — For nearly two centuries, a small Irish town has lured singletons to a festival every September that sees hopeful romantics seek their one true love. The monthlong matchmaking festival that started in 1857 has become a global event , attracting over 60,000 visitors annually to the rugged landscape of County Clare, and specifically to the tiny town of Lisdoonvarna. The festival even broke into American pop culture, featuring several years ago on the sitcom "Schitt's Creek." In many ways, it's an old-world solution to modern dating. There is no app and no algorithms, just a chance to meet a match organically, through Irish traditional dancing and music, speed dating — or through the matchmaking skills of 83-year-old local legend Willie Daly. Daly's grandfather helped start the festival, and his family has been pairing couples for three generations. In his father's and grandfather's day, many Irish towns and villages had traditional matchmakers, but Daly is now believed to be among the last, if not the last, keeping the tradition alive.

items.text: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
items.article: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions. US convicted murderer Christa Pike is in hospital and being given "life-saving measures" after Tennessee authorities failed in their attempt to execute her by lethal injection. The case of Pike, whose attempted execution had already been the subject of a high-profile legal battle, has raised a number of questions. These include what went wrong, what happens next, and - for opponents of the death penalty - fresh concerns around the suffering of an inmate when an execution does not go to plan. A review into what happened has been ordered and executions in Tennessee have been halted for the rest of the year, Governor Bill Lee said. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, an attack that was perpetrated alongside her then-boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp. She was scheduled to be put to death on Wednesday evening, local time. The injections were allowed by the US Supreme Court at the eleventh hour after the legal battle.

items.article: President Donald Trump may sign a bill into law that would change the way Social Security retirement ages are described. One of the biggest decisions retirees make — when to claim Social Security benefits — would be described differently under a bill that may soon become law. The Claiming Age Clarity Act , a bipartisan bill that changes certain terms to describe the ages when a worker may claim Social Security retirement benefits, passed the Senate on Tuesday. The bill is now on its way to President Donald Trump for his signature. The White House did not respond to CNBC.com's request for comment on whether and when he might sign. Claiming Social Security benefits at age 62 — when qualifying retirees first become eligible — may permanently reduce benefits by up to 30% compared with claiming at full retirement age. By waiting until age 67, individuals born in 1960 or later may receive 100% of the benefits they've earned. And for each year delayed past that "full" retirement age, up to age 70, prospective beneficiaries receive an 8% benefit boost. The Claiming Age Clarity Act calls for modernizing the terminology around those claiming ages to help retirees better understand the trade-offs of their decisions. It does not change the claiming ages themselves or how benefits are paid.
